core_obligations: (a)-(b) is part of the definition; (a)-(e) and (a)-(f) are parts (2) and (1) of the delivered implies-lemma; hence (a)-(g) (proof lines 2989-2997).

(c) implies (b) is clear; (b) implies (c) by taking the coproduct diagram $h = \coprod h_x$, $a = \coprod a_x$, $b = \coprod b_x$, noting $h$ has $\mathcal{P}$ because $\mathcal{P}$ is smooth local on the target (proof lines 2997-3008).

(d): if (a) holds, $X \times_Y V \to V$ has $\mathcal{P}$ by smooth base change and $U \to V$ has $\mathcal{P}$ by smooth precomposition; conversely (d) with $U = X$, $V = Y$ gives (a) (proof lines 3008-3017).
proof_roadmap: Settle (a), (b), (e), (f), (g) via the definition and the implies-lemma.
Handle the (d) equivalence with base-change stability and precomposition stability.
difficulty_reason: Seven conditions (a)-(g) are shown equivalent: the definition handles (a)-(b); the delivered implies-lemma handles (a)-(e) and (a)-(f), from which (a)-(g) follows; the (b)-(c) equivalence assembles a global diagram as a coproduct of the local witnesses (using smooth locality on the target to keep $h$ in $\mathcal{P}$); and the (d) equivalence uses stability under smooth base change and smooth precomposition.
